`url_fetcher.fetch(url, allowed_hosts, opener=None)` (see seed/README.md) is how our scrapers pull data from a configured allowlist of partner hosts. It calls `opener(url)` (which defaults to a real HTTP GET, but every caller in the test suite passes a fake one) and returns whatever bytes come back. The host check was written for the happy path and is sloppy — we're about to point it at user-suggested URLs, so please harden it:

- Only `http` and `https` URLs may be fetched (the scheme match is case-insensitive); anything else (`file:`, `ftp:`, `javascript:`, a URL with no host at all, …) must raise `url_fetcher.URLSecurityError`.
- A URL that embeds credentials (`user:pass@host` or `user@host` right before the hostname) must be rejected outright, even if the host after the `@` is itself allowlisted.
- The host must match an entry in `allowed_hosts` exactly and case-insensitively (treating a single trailing dot as insignificant, since `example.com.` and `example.com` name the same thing) — don't be fooled by a host that merely contains, starts with, or ends with an allowed name. There's no implicit subdomain access either: `sub.example.com` is only fetchable if it is itself listed in `allowed_hosts`. The port, if any, doesn't affect the match.
- `opener` can raise `url_fetcher.Redirect(location)` to signal a 3xx response. When that happens, validate `location` exactly like any other URL before ever calling `opener` with it — never follow a redirect to a URL that wouldn't itself pass the allowlist. Follow at most 3 redirects; if it's still redirecting after that, raise `URLSecurityError` instead of looping forever.
- Keep the boring case boring: a plain allowlisted `http`/`https` URL with no redirect should still fetch in exactly one `opener` call.
